page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-c48g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by the x86_64 architecture on a KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The CPU subsystem includes 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and support for AVX-512 vector extensions including AVX-512 VNNI. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Ampere A10 GPU equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. System memory totals 310 GB, providing an allocation of 6.46 GB per vCPU, while baseline network throughput is rated at 16 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive throughput in specialized GPU and multi-core processing tasks. Large language model inference yields top-tier performance for small and medium model architectures, delivering 9,711.08 prompt processing tokens per second on a 135M model and 90.44 generation tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. CPU-bound throughput sits within the middle tiers across general compute suites, recorded at 47,330.47 in PassMark CPU score and 15,234.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Cryptographic routines and parallel decompression perform well above median, supported by dedicated hardware instructions that achieve 42,228.64 in PassMark CPU encryption and 230.87 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The hardware configuration trades local high-speed disk arrays for a balanced compute-to-GPU topology paired with substantial system RAM. Because local scratch storage is absent, workflows demanding extreme local disk I/O require remote storage volumes, which introduces reliance on the 16 Gbps network interface. The instance delivers high resource density for graphics virtualization, video processing, AI inference, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.

The ecs.gn7i-c48g1.12xlarge is suited for deep learning inference workloads involving small to mid-sized language models, GPU-accelerated video rendering, image processing, and distributed simulation environments requiring strong per-core memory capacity alongside dedicated NVIDIA Ampere acceleration.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides 16 Gbps of baseline networking without local storage. This configuration fits deep learning inference, image and video processing pipelines, and data-intensive compute workloads requiring dedicated GPU acceleration.
